packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-20 - unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this text.
Rule note: I ran one `ls` on the three packet directories to learn the image filenames; that listing showed that packet.json exists. I did not open packet.json or anything else.

== image-001.jpg (overview, reduced, face 1) ==
Layout survey (observation): a small upright rectangular scrap, c. 4.3 cm wide by c. 5.5 cm high against the ruler, on black felt. The surface is dark grey (stained or darkened; material not determinable from the image - could be parchment or paper). Writing is horizontal and upright in this frame, in a small, quick cursive hand in dark ink with long abbreviation strokes. This face is largely blank or effaced: writing survives only (a) as a trace at the very top left edge, (b) in a band of c. 5 lines across the middle (c. 1.3-2.5 cm from the top), which seems to stand in two blocks - a narrow left block and a wider right block separated by a faint vertical line c. 4 mm from the left edge (tentative: main column with a marginal note, or two columns), and (c) in c. 3 lines at the bottom right. Some words in the middle band are struck through with a horizontal line (observation; tentative: deletions) or underlined. No colour, rubrics, initials or running titles visible.

== image-002.jpg (the only tile for face 1; the scrap fills the tile at c. 570 px width, i.e. roughly 13 px per mm) ==
At this resolution individual letters are 3-5 px; I can report word shapes only.

Nothing on this face is read securely enough to quote.

== image-003.jpg (overview, reduced, face 2) ==
Observation: the other face of the same scrap (same size and outline, mirrored). This face is fully written: c. 15 long lines across the whole width, single column, same small cursive hand with frequent superscript abbreviation strokes and long descenders; lines run to both cut edges, so beginnings and ends of lines are probably lost (tentative). After line 8 there is a short line (one word at the left) followed by a slightly wider interline - tentative: paragraph end, with a new paragraph starting at line 10. No colour, rubric, enlarged initial or underlining visible. Margins not preserved; a crop this small cannot show the page layout.

== Selected / unread / limitations (packet-20) ==
- I attempted every visible line on both faces; none is read with confidence. The gaps here reflect the image scale and the dark, low-contrast surface, not a lack of looking: each face was supplied as one tile of c. 570 x 700 px for a 4.3 x 5.5 cm scrap, so the x-height of this cursive is about 3 px. The "tile" is effectively the same resolution as the overview.
- No heading, question opening, lemma, citation formula or numeral could be isolated. The words offered with "?" are shape-guesses with several alternatives and are not fit for source matching.
- Secure observations only: single small scrap, two faces; face 2 fully written in one column of c. 15-16 lines of abbreviated cursive with a probable paragraph break after l.8/9; face 1 mostly blank or effaced with a c. 5-line entry (possibly with marginal note and cancelled words) and c. 3 lines at the foot. The uneven, note-like disposition of face 1 suggests (tentatively) casual entries or a document/notes rather than a ruled book page, but I cannot confirm this.
- Language: the abbreviation habits and the few word shapes look Latin (tentative).
- Needed for a real reading: native-resolution tiles (at least 4-5x the present scale), ideally infrared or raking/contrast-enhanced, of face 2 lines 1-8 and 10-16, and of the middle band of face 1.
- Line ends at both sides are cut; line order top-to-bottom is as given; which face is recto is unknown.
- This is an unverified image reading.
